title: Multiple global change factors alter the scaling of nitrogen to phosphorus in alpine plants
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

The stoichiometry and allometry of nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) reflect nutrient absorption and dynamic allocation by plants, and can be regulated by global change factors (e.g. nitrogen enrichment, climate warming and altered precipitation). Yet, how multiple global change factors act interactively to influence the stoichiometric characteristics of N and P and their scaling relationships in different plant organs remains poorly understood. In a field experiment with treatments of nitrogen addition (Nadd), warming (W) and reduced precipitation (Pr) in an alpine meadow, we examined how global change factors interact to alter N and P stoichiometric characteristics of leaves and seeds. An allometry model (i.e. N = βP α ) was employed to detect changes in the scaling of plant N to P under different treatments. Our results showed that nitrogen addition significantly increased leaf N concentration (+44.0%), seed N concentration (+16.9%) and leaf N:P ratios (+27.8%) under ambient temperatures and significantly increased leaf N concentration (+53.7%) and leaf N:P ratios (+46.4%) under ambient precipitation. Importantly, nitrogen addition and warming (or reduced precipitation) had synergistic effects on P concentration of leaves and seeds, and antagonistic effects on N:P ratios of leaves. Moreover, although none of the three global change factors individually altered the scaling of N to P, nitrogen addition interacted with warming or with reduced precipitation to decrease the scaling exponents in leaves and increase them in seeds. Our results suggest that multiple global change factors can alter the N and P allocation patterns and result in decoupling of N and P in different plant organs. These findings highlight the importance of considering interactions of multiple factors when predicting dynamic changes in plant stoichiometric characteristics and nutrient utilization strategies under global change scenarios.

摘要

氮(N)、磷(P)的化学计量特征和异速生长关系反映了植物对养分的吸收和动态分配过程, 并且这些过程受到全球变化因子(例如氮富集、气候变暖和降水改变)的调控。然而, 多个全球变化因子将如何相互作用影响植物N和P在不同器官中的化学计量特征及其异速生长关系尚不清楚。 本研究利用在青藏高原高寒草甸设置的包含氮添加(Nadd)、增温(W)和减雨(Pr)处理的野外试验, 探究了全球变化因子如何交互式地改变叶片和种子中N和P的化学计量特征。并采用了异速生长模型(即N = βPα)来探讨不同处理下植物N和P之间的异速关系变化。 研究发现, 在环境温度下, 氮添加显著增加了叶片N含量(+44.0%)、种子N含量(+16.9%)和叶片N:P比(+27.8%)；而在环境降水下, 氮添加显著增加了叶片N含量(+53.7%)和叶片N:P比(+46.4%)。当氮添加和增温/减雨共同处理时, 对叶片和种子的P含量产生协同作用, 对叶片N:P比产生拮抗作用。此外, 三个全球变化因子单独处理时, 均不会改变植物N和P之间的异速关系, 但是, 氮添加与增温或减雨的交互处理导致了叶片的N和P异速指数(异速生长模型取对数之后的回归斜率)降低, 种子的N和P异速指数增加。 本研究表明, 多个全球变化因子将改变N和P的异速分配模式, 并导致N和P在不同植物器官中发生解耦现象。以上结果进一步强调了在全球变化情境下, 预测植物化学计量特征和养分利用策略的动态变化时, 需要考虑多个全球变化因子的交互作用。
